title: Drug Sensitivity and Allele Specificity of First-Line Osimertinib Resistance EGFR Mutations.
abstract: Osimertinib, a mutant-specific third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is emerging as the preferred first-line therapy for EGFR -mutant lung cancer, yet resistance inevitably develops in patients.

We modeled acquired resistance to osimertinib in transgenic mouse models of EGFR L858R -induced lung adenocarcinoma and found that it is mediated largely through secondary mutations in EGFR -either C797S or L718V/Q.
Analysis of circulating free DNA data from patients revealed that L718Q/V mutations almost always occur in the context of an L858R driver mutation.
Therapeutic testing in mice revealed that both erlotinib and afatinib caused regression of osimertinib-resistant C797S-containing tumors, whereas only afatinib was effective on L718Q mutant tumors.
Combination first-line osimertinib plus erlotinib treatment prevented the emergence of secondary mutations in EGFR .

These findings highlight how knowledge of the specific characteristics of resistance mutations is important for determining potential subsequent treatment approaches and suggest strategies to overcome or prevent osimertinib resistance in vivo .
SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides insight into the biological and molecular properties of osimertinib resistance EGFR mutations and evaluates therapeutic strategies to overcome resistance.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)-associated mutations in exons encoding the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) of EGFR confer sensitivity to 1st and 2nd generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) such as erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib and dacomitinib (); however, almost all patients develop acquired resistance to these drugs about one year after starting treatment.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: About 60% of these resistant tumors have a secondary mutation in exon 20 (T790M), which increases the ATP-binding affinity of the mutated protein and renders the tumor resistant to 1st and 2nd generation TKIs ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Several other mechanisms of acquired resistance to TKIs have been identified, such as mutations in genes encoding proteins that signal downstream of EGFR, histological transformation, and amplification of other receptor tyrosine kinases ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Third generation inhibitors (e.g. osimertinib) were developed that target mutated EGFR (including the T790M mutation) over wild-type, presumably resulting in decreased toxicity ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Based on its clinical activity, osimertinib was first approved for the second-line treatment of T790M-positive EGFR mutant lung cancer ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: However, resistance to second-line osimertinib has also been described in patients - and in ~30% of cases is due to the emergence of additional mutations in EGFR such as C797S/G, G796S/R, L792F/H, L718Q/V, and G724S (-).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: The C797S mutation removes the cysteine side-chain with which osimertinib reacts covalently, thus preventing drug binding to EGFR.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Mutations at L718 and G796 have been predicted to prevent drug binding by sterically altering the drug-binding pocket (, ).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Osimertinib has also shown promising activity in the first-line (, ), leading to its recent approval for use in this setting.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: This raises important questions concerning likely mechanisms of resistance to first-line osimertinib, about which very little is known.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in patients whose tumors progressed on first-line osimertinib (, ) has shown that MET amplification was the most common mechanism of resistance (14%), followed by the C797S (7%) and L718Q EGFR mutations (2% of cases).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Given this limited information, it remains unclear which therapeutic strategies might be effective at overcoming resistance to first-line osimertinib.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: One possible strategy is to sequentially apply, or combine, different generations of EGFR TKIs.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Several studies have demonstrated that a 1st generation TKI is effective in cell line models with C797S (, ), and this is supported by case reports of several patients who responded to treatment with a 1st generation EGFR TKI (, ) or the combination of osimertinib plus a 1st generation EGFR TKI () after developing resistance to osimertinib mediated by C797S.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Indeed, a clinical trial is currently underway to evaluate the combination of osimertinib and gefitinib in TKI-naïve EGFR mutant lung cancer patients [NCT03122717].

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Similarly, several in vitro studies and one case report have suggested that 2nd generation TKIs can be effective in cells that have acquired osimertinib resistance through acquisition of an L718 mutation (, , , ).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: To investigate mechanisms of resistance to first-line osimertinib more exhaustively, we used a genetically-engineered mouse model (GEMM) of EGFR mutant lung cancer to generate osimertinib-resistant tumors and evaluate the efficacy of sequential or combination EGFR TKIs to overcome or prevent resistance.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Further, we analyzed mutational data obtained from a large cohort of lung cancer patients and uncovered allele specificity of osimertinib resistance EGFR mutations.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Finally, we report a case of a patient with a tumor harboring both the L718V and L718Q mutations at resistance to first-line osimertinib who benefited from afatinib treatment.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The mean progression-free survival for osimertinib in the first-line is 19 months, with an overall survival of 39 months, which is superior to that observed with other TKIs (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Patients are not cured, however, and a better understanding of acquired resistance to osimertinib is needed.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Here, using GEMMs of EGFR mutant LUAD, we show that resistance to first-line osimertinib can be due to acquired C797S, L718Q and L718V mutations in EGFR.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This is the first report of an in vivo first-line osimertinib resistance model that acquires EGFR mutations.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Data emerging from the FLAURA trial of front-line osimertinib indicate that, at acquired resistance, the C797S and L718Q mutations are detected in 7% and 2% of cases from ctDNA ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The higher frequency of C797S mutations versus L718Q mutations observed in these patient samples (with a variety of driver mutations) compared with the more equal distribution of C797S and L718Q mutations in our mouse model may reflect the allele specificity of the resistance mutations.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Indeed, our analysis of cfDNA from patients with EGFR mutant lung cancer clearly show that C797S mutations predominate in the Del19 subset of tumors, and that L718Q and L718V mutations generally only arise in the context of L858R, consistent with the few published reports of L718Q/V mutations (-, , , ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Why L718Q/V mutations are found more readily in the context of L858R mutations in patients remains to be determined.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It is possible that it is due to differential stability of the different mutation combinations or differences in other biochemical properties such as their kinase activity or dimerization properties.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Interestingly, in vitro data in our study and others’ () show that Del19 cells harboring a L718Q/V mutation can exist and are resistant to osimertinib suggesting the intriguing possibility that resistance mechanisms that emerge spontaneously in vivo may be somewhat different than those observed in vitro.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The mechanism by which the C797S substitution causes osimertinib resistance is straightforward as it removes the side-chain thiol with which osimertinib reacts covalently.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Models obtained using molecular dynamics-based energy minimization provide some insight into how L718V/Q mutations might affect drug-binding.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The L718 side-chain contacts the phenyl ring of the drug in a crystal structure of osimertinib-bound wild-type EGFR TKD (PDB ID 4ZAU) ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Substituting L718 with V or Q is therefore highly likely to alter the mode or orientation of osimertinib binding, as others have noted (, , ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: We confirmed this by modeling non-covalent complexes of L858R-mutated EGFR TKD with osimertinib, erlotinib, and afatinib (Figure 7).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: While the pose of osimertinib in the energy-minimized L858R TKD complex (with leucine at position 718) is maintained, loss of van der Waals interactions is seen for the L718V mutation, and a steric clash with the glutamine side-chain is seen for the L718Q mutation (upper panels, Figure 7).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: These effects are compensated for in the models by reorientation of osimertinib in the drug-binding site, which may make its orientation sub-optimal for covalent reaction with C797 - as argued previously for L718Q/T790M EGFR ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: There is also some reduction in osimertinib binding energy suggesting that the affinity of the ‘encounter complex’ prior to covalent reaction may be reduced - which would also reduce efficacy.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The same mutations are predicted to have similar effects on erlotinib binding energy and orientation (middle panel, Figure 7).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: In this case, the lack of any covalent aspect suggests that observed resistance must arise from weakened binding.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Indeed, L718 contacts erlotinib directly in EGFR/erlotinib crystal structures ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Finally, the effects of the L718V/Q mutations on afatinib binding energy are only ~80% of those calculated for osimertinib, suggesting that they will have less severe effects on residence time of afatinib for its covalent reaction.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Moreover, the orientation of afatinib appears less affected by the mutations - in Figure 7, there is no clash between afatinib in its L858R-bound orientation and the Q718 side-chain, although interactions with L718 are lost in the L718V variant.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Through experiments in CRISPR-edited human EGFR mutant LUAD cell lines - to mimic the acquisition of resistance when low frequency sub-clonal mutations are present - we show that sub-clonal L718V/Q mutations confer resistance to osimertinib.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: However, the L718V mutation retained some sensitivity to osimertinib at higher doses, and its frequency was reduced in vivo with higher osimertinib doses.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: The only three reports of patient tumor biopsies revealing an L718V mutation also coincided with loss of T790M (, , ), which was replicated in one of our mice and the CRISPR-edited PC9-VanR cells that gained L718V/Q mutations.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It is possible that destabilization of EGFR by L718 mutations prevents them from occurring in the presence of T790M.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: With osimertinib now as the preferred first-line therapy for advanced EGFR mutant tumors, it is critical to develop strategies to overcome resistance.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Our findings confirm the erlotinib-sensitivity of C797S mutant tumors in vivo, suggested by several in vitro studies and case reports (, , ), but L718V/Q mutant tumors were not sensitive to erlotinib.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Afatinib caused tumor regression in all tumors harboring C797S or L718Q mutations, as seen in previous in vitro studies (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: These data are consistent with our report of a patient who developed resistance to first-line osimertinib through the acquisition of both L718Q and L718V mutations in the tumor and whose disease was stabilized by afatinib treatment, similarly to two recent second-line osimertinib case reports with L858R+L718Q () and L858R+L718V mutant tumors ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Afatinib is currently FDA-approved for the treatment of tumors harboring G719X mutations based on its clinical efficacy (), suggesting a similar mechanism could underlie the sensitivity of L718 and G719 mutants to afatinib.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It is unclear why L718 mutations have never been observed in patient tumors resistant to 1st generation EGFR TKIs, given that they confer resistance to these inhibitors in vitro and in vivo based on our work and others’ (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It is possible that this could in part be due to the specific sensitivity of different alleles depending on the baseline mutation present.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Moreover, whether a mutation emerges may depend on several factors including the ease with which a mutation occurs (i.e. base change requirements), the strength of TKI-binding and the extent of the selective pressure exerted by the TKI.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Thus, a combination of EGFR TKIs may be able to prevent secondary EGFR mutations from emerging or delay the emergence of resistance.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: We tested the approach of combining a 1st and 3rd generation TKI in vivo and, importantly, none of the ten resistant tumors that developed had acquired mutations in EGFR.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: However, resistance did emerge.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Therefore, it is possible that by effectively suppressing EGFR-dependent mechanisms of resistance with the combination therapy, EGFR-independent mechanisms will become more prominent.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: How this will affect clinical outcomes for patients remains to be determined.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Indeed, clinical studies to evaluate the safety and efficacy of combination EGFR TKIs are ongoing (e.g. NCT03122717).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Given that we observed toxicities of the drug combination in vivo, future experiments with optimized doses of the agents will be important to conclusively determine whether this approach can be used to prevent EGFR-dependent resistance mechanisms.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This also highlights the importance of dose optimization to minimize toxicities and maximize efficacy in clinical trials.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Nevertheless, our data present an encouraging new therapeutic approach to treat EGFR mutant tumors upfront when tumors are most likely to be maximally addicted to mutant EGFR signaling.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Not all EGFR TKI-resistant tumors acquire secondary mutations in EGFR, and we identified Kras mutations in osimertinib-resistant tumors.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This is not surprising given that we previously observed these mutations arising in TKI-naïve tumors and at resistance to other EGFR inhibitors in these models (, , ), and activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway has been described as a mechanism of resistance to 3rd generation EGFR TKIs (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Whether the relatively high abundance of Kras mutations in our mouse model is due to spontaneous tumor development in aging mice () or whether these are enriched with osimertinib requires additional investigation.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Nevertheless, KRAS mutations are certainly of clinical relevance given that they are being observed at osimertinib resistance in patients (-, , ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Acquired EGFR and Kras mutations account for almost all cases of osimertinib-resistant GEMM tumors described here.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: However, other mechanisms of resistance have been observed in patients (, , , ) and overall, secondary mutations in EGFR are found more frequently in our mouse models than in osimertinib-resistant human tumors.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This could reflect the reduced genomic complexity of the GEMM tumors (), and the fact that expression of the mutant EGFR transgene is constantly being driven by the presence of doxycycline, which may confer a greater propensity for on-target resistance.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Therefore, other models should be used for further discovery of EGFR-independent resistance mechanisms and evaluation of therapeutic approaches to overcome them (, , ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Nonetheless, our study provides important insight into EGFR-dependent (and proximal) resistance mechanisms to osimertinib and highlights the complexity and heterogeneity of osimertinib resistance.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Two key avenues for clinical investigation suggested by our findings are: i).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Evaluation of sequential TKI treatment that includes osimertinib followed by a 2nd generation TKI such as afatinib or dacomitinib, and ii).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Evaluation of TKI combinations in the first-line.
